stemBlocks.value: A supermarket sells cereal as 500 g for $480, 750 g for $690, and 1 kg for $920. (a) Calculate the cost per gram for each size. (b) Which size is the best buy? (c) How much would it cost to buy 3 kg using the best option?
Think first: Convert 1 kg to 1 000 g first so all three sizes are measured in the same unit before you divide.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p025-q30 from workbook page 25.

Find the cost per gram of the 750 g box.
Convert 1 kg to grams and find its cost per gram.

contentBlocks.value: Result: the 750 g and 1 kg boxes tie as best

solutionSteps.instruction: Cost 3 kg at the best rate.

contentBlocks.value: 3 000 g x $0.92, that is three 1 kg boxes at $920 or four 750 g boxes at $690

strategyBlocks.value: Divide each price by its mass in grams, compare the three costs per gram, then buy 3 kg using whichever size is cheapest.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) 500 g: $0.96 per g; 750 g: $0.92 per g; 1 kg: $0.92 per g  (b) the 750 g and the 1 kg boxes are equally the best buy at $0.92 per g, both beating the 500 g box  (c) 3 kg costs $2 760

whyThisWorks.value: Comparing rates only works when the units match, so the kilogram must become 1 000 g before dividing. Two offers with the same unit cost are genuinely equal value, and 3 kg is a whole number of boxes either way, so both routes cost $2 760. The smallest box being dearest per gram is the usual pattern for packaged goods.

examTip.value: Convert every measurement to the same unit before any division. A mixed kg and g comparison is the fastest way to lose an easy mark.
